Messages.Body:
Hello fierce methuselahs !
After last year Covid-caused cancelling, we are happy to announce that the annual Lille Easter Tournament will take place.
Unfortunately it will be a Lackey one, but the good side is that even our fellow clanmates and allies from the New World can join us.
It's a free tournament and thanks to our generous sponsors (Asmodée & Black Chantry Productions) there will be promos for the first 20 players and Keyforge decks for everyone.
Of course French players will get them at Easter 2022 but for those who really want their prizes (French and foreigners alike) I am sure we will be able to send them with Mondial Relay / Punto Pack or any postal service that works (against a little fee of course, even Gangrel have to pay the electricity and internet bills  )

I have 72 Keyforge decks and here is the promo distribution :

Finalists will get a random Baron and 1 Nefertiti Adv.
From 6 to 10 : 2 Barons
From 11 to 15 : 3 Barons
From 16 to 20 : 4 Barons

Nefertiti Advanced for players ranked 7th, 11th, 18th and last.

It will be a 3R+F, with a 2 hour time limit.
The schedule (French time) is

R1 : saturday 3 pm
R2 : sunday 10 am
R3 : sunday 1 pm
Final : sunday evening 6 pm (or whatever suits the finalists)

If all players at a table have a mic and Discord access et they can decide to use it. If not, the Lackey chat box should be enough.

Please register here with your vekn number.
www.vekn.fr/forum/viewtopic.php?f=27&t=19608

Messages.Author: Vlad

Update

If 11 or less players, we will play an Adaptability tournament

3.1.5 Multi-Deck System
Players are prohibited from making modifications to their decks between rounds unless the tournament uses the following multi-deck rules. The multi-deck system can be used at any tournament with fewer than 12 players (i.e., fewer than three tables). Organizers choosing to use this system must announce its use in advance of the tournament date. Players may choose to bring any number of tournament-legal decks to the tournament and/or extra cards to exchange with cards in their decks (also known as a sideboard in some games). Between rounds, players may freely switch decks (or cards in their decks). A tournament begun with the multi-deck system cannot admit more players between rounds if doing so would create a round with 12 or more players.
